> A neopixel clock that has neopixels around it to tell the time and an OLED display to show the current date, with 3 switches to switch modes and time zones. It retrieves the date and time using the XIAO ESP32-C3 to get it using API keys over Wi-Fi. I will use micropython for the code.

### 2026-11-05: In this session, I finished replacing and rewiring the schematic after adding 60 LED's instead of 36. Then I placed all of the LED's in a circle. Afterwards, I changed the capacitors to the ones match

**2.75h**

In this session, I finished replacing and rewiring the schematic after adding 60 LED's instead of 36. Then I placed all of the LED's in a circle. Afterwards, I changed the capacitors to the ones matching to the through hole ones I found on AliExpress. Finally, I wired the LED's to each other, making sure I had the correct track width, spacing, via size, etc.

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/199346b5-6aad-4cf0-9c06-0b7e0b573f71/video.mp4)

### 2026-11-07: For this session, I was mainly swapping parts to fit within the budget, but I also placed the OLED pin headers on the PCB, which I did first.

**2.98h**

For this session, I was mainly swapping parts to fit within the budget, but I also placed the OLED pin headers on the PCB, which I did first.

I used AI to try to find the exact dimensions the headers should be relative to the silkscreen, but then I realized that it didn't have to be placed exactly on the silkscreen.

After that, I had to try and find parts that cost less to fit the BOM's budget, because when I got the price of the PCB from JLCPCB, I realized that it cost more than I thought it would and I would have to swap out some parts. I swapped out the XIAO ESP32C3 for the ESP32C3 Super Mini since it was cheaper on AliExpress. Then I swapped the 2.42" OLED for the same OLED I used for Week 4 since it was cheaper and I didn't have to find another part. Even that wasn't enough, so I chose the most expensive thing on my BOM after that other than the PCB, which was the pack of resistors from AliExpress. I tried many options as a replacement, but the shipping or the unit price made it too expensive. I thought I was going to have to settle for 2 ~$2.50 packs for each resistor value and probably have to cut the price on another part, which would be very difficult since all of them past that were < $5, but then AI found gold with a ~$2.50 pack of 300 which included both resistor values and more, and the shipping cost was free. I just hope it isn't a scam.

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/5db3fa08-81ff-4d7c-801a-edb09b811a59/video.mp4)
